research_updates.title: Taxpayer accounts and incentive agreements
research_updates.notes: City summary reviewed September 3, 2026: Google is identified with Design LLC. The county lists GOOGLE LLC and DESIGN LLC as separate taxpayer parties; their bills and assessed values are shown separately below. The city describes the first EZ abatement as expired and later EZ and SIP agreements as continuing. Property tax bills do not include a verified accounting of all negotiated fees or incentives, and are not evidence of cash collected. Parcel-level linkage remains unresolved.

source.title: Enterprise Zone & Strategic Investment Program Agreements with Google
source.notes: Undated city summary reviewed September 3, 2026. Identifies Google with Design LLC and links county top-taxpayer reports. Separates EZ agreements from the 2021 SIP agreement and distinguishes initial payments, property tax, Community Service Fee and Guaranteed Annual Payment. Its projected aggregate EZ payments are not treated as actual receipts.

research_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — historical campus and later SIP projects separated
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Google location and archive materials; Business Oregon commission packets, resolutions SIP-21-01 and SIP-21-02, and program tables; City planning records SPR 512-22 and SPR 538-23; and contractor project pages for 2005-2026. Queries used Google, Design LLC, Moraine Industries, GOR, River Road, 3500 River Road, tax lots 700 and 200, SIP-21-01, SIP-21-02, SPR 512-22 and SPR 538-23. Sources support the 2006 opening, 2015 fourth-building start, a December 2021 three-facility snapshot, two separately bounded SIP projects, and later roughly 289,000-square-foot River Road applications. They do not establish that the two SIP forecasts were fully realized or map every tax account, permit and inventory point to one building.

source.title: Google data centers — The Dalles, Oregon
source.notes: The operator page says Google opened its first owned-and-operated data center in The Dalles in 2006 and began building a fourth data center in 2015. Current investment, grant and volunteer totals are reported for Oregon rather than the selected campus or Wasco County and therefore are not normalized as project records.

research_updates.title: Fiscal audit — tax bills preserved; realized incentive cost and fiscal net unresolved
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Wasco County assessor/top-taxpayer reports for tax years 2022-2025; county BOCC minutes from 2021-2022; City tax-agreement pages and FY 2024-2025/FY 2025-2026 budgets; Business Oregon SIP applications, commission packets, statutory tables and resolutions; and Oregon tax-program materials. Searches used Google LLC party 155421, Design LLC party 130136, SIP-21-01, SIP-21-02, enterprise zone, community service fee, GAP, tax saved, tax paid and exempt value. The baseline six bills and six assessments remain unchanged. Agreements and budgets publish formulas and negotiated payments, but no reconciled realized abatement ledger, payment-status proof for the billed series, recipient-level distribution, same-scope marginal public-service cost or defensible net fiscal result was found; formulas and the approximately $1.9 billion 2021 exempt-value snapshot are not converted to tax savings.

research_updates.title: Construction and procurement audit — six permit valuations retained without summation
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: City of The Dalles HPRM planning files and agenda packets; Oregon ePermitting identifiers; BuildZoom's public permit summary; OSHA inspection 1832411.015; Whiting-Turner, Largo Concrete, Jacobs, KPFF and Harder Mechanical project or licensing pages; Port of The Dalles packets and lease references; and general contractor/supplier searches for 2021-2026. Exact searches covered 3500 River Road, GOR1A, GOR2A, 921-24-001277-PLM, 921-25-000109-PLM, 921-25-000303-MECH, 921-25-000304-MECH, 921-25-000313-MECH and 921-25-000314-MECH. Six issued administrative valuations are retained individually. No official downloadable project-wide permit ledger, contract value, invoice, audited construction outlay, worker hours, payroll, vendor payment, supplier geography or local-retention share was found; overlapping work descriptions prevent summation.

source.title: Harder Mechanical Contractors — public permit summary for 3500 River Road
source.notes: The contractor profile reproduces Oregon permit identifiers, issue dates, work descriptions, status and administrative valuations for Harder Mechanical work at 3500 River Road. Six issued phase-specific 2024-2025 permits are retained individually as reported permit values. They may overlap within the broader building program and are not invoices, audited spending, local procurement, economic output or an additive project total.

research_updates.title: Resource and environmental audit — campus allocation remains unavailable
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Northern Wasco County PUD board/news/tariff materials; Oregon Public Utility Commission jurisdiction information; Oregon Department of Energy Data Center Advisory Committee records; City water-infrastructure disclosures and budgets; Google's The Dalles water profile and 2024 Oregon impact study; Oregon DEQ environmental records and permit searches; and EPA facility searches for 2005-2026. Queries used Google, Design LLC, 3500 River Road, data center, substation, Taylor Lake, load, kWh, water, wastewater, ASR, emissions, generator and air permit. The baseline $28.5 million water-infrastructure record remains. Public sources disclose utility-system load and Oregon-level water consumption/PUE, but no customer tariff, campus annual electricity, project-attributable substation cost, selected-building water allocation, wastewater discharge, generator inventory or campus emissions. Direct actual water and PUE also lack matching evidence metrics, so those figures are not relabeled as projections or capacity.

source.title: Data Center Advisory Committee facilitator meeting summary — May 29, 2026
source.notes: The official summary reports that Northern Wasco County PUD serves three data-center campuses and that its total system load rose from 90 MW in January 2016 to 277 MW in January 2026, driven substantially by data centers. Because neither load nor infrastructure cost is customer-allocated, no Google-campus electricity, tariff, utility investment or public-cost record is created.

research_updates.title: Workforce audit — dated headcount added; payroll and residence remain gaps
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Business Oregon employment/payroll material; Google careers and operator location pages; WorkSource/first-source hiring references in SIP records; Oregon workforce reports; and local education/workforce recipient records for 2005-2026. Queries used Google The Dalles, Design LLC, employees, contractors, vendors, salary, payroll, FTE, first source, apprenticeship and job titles. The December 2021 approximately 120 Google employees and nearly 400 onsite contractor/vendor jobs are retained as distinct campus stocks. Live vacancies and salary ranges are not filled positions or realized payroll. No current facility headcount, occupation table, annual payroll, hours, turnover, employee residence, local-hire realization or building allocation was found.

source.title: Google Careers — The Dalles data-center openings
source.notes: The reviewed listing is for a Data Center Electrical Engineer in The Dalles and discloses a salary range. A current vacancy and offered range do not establish a filled campus position, annual payroll, employee residence, average realized wage or retention; no quantitative record is created.

research_updates.title: Community audit — one recipient-verified local grant added
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Google community and location disclosures; Columbia Gorge Community College board materials; North Wasco County School District and Columbia Gorge ESD records; The Dalles-Wasco County Library and local nonprofit pages; city/county budget references; and recipient searches for grants, gifts, robotics, STEM, education, housing and volunteer support from 2006-2026. CGCC verifies receipt of a $50,000 Google grant for its The Dalles simulation lab. Other operator totals are statewide, cumulative, undated, co-funded or lack a recipient ledger and are not allocated to the campus. No complete annual Wasco County grant register, in-kind valuation or campus-attributable volunteer-hour series was found.

source.title: Columbia Gorge Community College Board minutes — August 2024
source.notes: The recipient's board minutes report receipt of a $50,000 Google grant dedicated to an updated simulation lab under construction at the college's The Dalles campus. This recipient-verified transfer is retained separately from statewide Google philanthropy totals and from negotiated tax-agreement payments.

research_updates.title: Investment and supplier audit — cumulative actual separated from forecasts
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Business Oregon project/company material; Google operator investment pages; City and county economic-development records; contractor portfolios; planning and permit records; and supplier/carrier/procurement searches from 2005-2026. The 2021 state memo supports approximately $5 billion cumulative investment in the three existing facilities and two separate approximately $600 million SIP project forecasts. Statewide current investment totals are excluded, and permit valuations are not substituted for expenditure. The nearly 400 onsite contractor/vendor jobs establish an operations stock only; no vendor roster, contract amount, local purchase share, supplier output, carrier payment, local payroll or audited equipment-versus-construction split was found.

source.title: Oregon Business Development Commission December 2021 packet — Google/The Dalles SIP projects
source.notes: The commission packet contains the December 10 staff memo and adopted SIP-21-01/SIP-21-02 resolutions. It reports a dated snapshot of three existing enterprise-zone facilities, approximately 120 Google employees, nearly 400 full-time onsite contractor/vendor jobs, and about $5 billion of cumulative investment. Each later SIP project is separately bounded, forecast at about $600 million and ten Google jobs, and capped at one contiguous complex with no more than a 500,000-square-foot footprint and 1,000,000 square feet of building area. The forecasts are not realized spending, employment, tax savings or public cost.

research_updates.title: Structured-data and modeling audit — only descriptive county benchmarks qualify
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: repository BEA/BLS County Economic Core panel for 2001-2024, facility-study county exclusions, and the project-specific direct-evidence categories documented above. The selected campus opened in 2006, leaving a five-year 2001-2005 pre-period in the available panel. After direct-source searches did not produce causal county outcomes, three reproducible inverse-distance-weighted 20-county comparison gaps are retained only as low-confidence descriptive context with fit-sensitivity envelopes. No input-output supplier, resource, construction-employment, public-cost, induced-household or net-fiscal model is eligible because project-specific expenditure, payroll, consumption and same-scope cost anchors are missing. No records requests were made.

source.title: County Economic Core Panel, 2001-2024
source.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
source.notes: Repository panel compiled from official annual county real GDP, total employment, and average-weekly-wage series. These are county observations, not project contributions; the retained comparison modules use them descriptively with explicit noncausal limitations.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Each benchmark uses the available 2001-2005 pre-opening history, excludes all study counties from a 20-county inverse-distance-weighted donor pool, and carries a fit-sensitivity envelope. No model converts broad investment or permit values to jobs, onsite contractor counts to supplier output, utility-system loads to campus consumption, tax bills to payments, or unmatched incentive formulas and public costs to a fiscal net.

project_description: Google's The Dalles data-center project is an operator-owned campus in The Dalles, Wasco County, Oregon, rather than one selected building or the company's statewide portfolio. Google opened its first owned-and-operated data center there in 2006 and began building a fourth in 2015; Business Oregon later described three existing enterprise-zone facilities and two separately bounded SIP projects on tax lots 700 and 200. City approvals at 3500 River Road document roughly 289,000-square-foot data-center buildings, while each SIP resolution caps its approved complex at a 500,000-square-foot footprint and 1,000,000 square feet of building area.
